transcript.content: Hi, welcome in — I'm Dr. [Name]. To start, can you tell me what's been bothering you or what brought you in to see me today?

Hi, Doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. Um... I hope I explain this right. I guess I'm here because I... well, I just don't really care about anything anymore. Which sounds terrible to say out loud, I know, and I'm sorry. 

I used to do a lot. I loved my art classes, and going to board-game nights, and hiking... I was even supposed to be getting back to my soccer team. But lately, I just... I don't have any interest in them. I end up just sitting in my room while everything kind of... slips away. I know I should be trying harder to get out and do things, so I feel awful about it. Is... is that the sort of thing you were asking about? I hope that makes sense.
How long have you been feeling this way—not caring about things you used to enjoy?

Um... well, it's been a little while. I really tried to just push through it, I promise I did. But it became... pretty constant around the summer before last. So, I guess it's been about a year and four months now? 

I know I should have come in way sooner, and I feel terrible for letting it go on this long without getting help. I just kept hoping I'd snap out of it so I wouldn't have to bother anyone with it. Is... is that the right kind of answer? I hope I'm giving you what you need.
Over these past 16 months, has this low mood and loss of interest been pretty much constant and unchanging day to day, or did it start as a noticeable shift from how you normally felt before?

Um... well, it definitely felt like a big shift from how I used to be at first. But since it started, it's been... yeah, pretty constant. 

I really try to start my mornings off right, I promise I do. I don't want to be a downer or just give up. But most days, I just wake up with this... this heavy, hollow feeling right in my chest. It almost feels like there's no future for me beyond my apartment walls. Which I know sounds so dramatic, and I'm really sorry to complain like this. I just... I can't seem to shake it no matter how hard I try. 

Did I explain that okay? I want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Over these past 16 months, has this affected your ability to keep up with daily responsibilities like work, self-care, or household tasks, or have you still been able to manage those most days?

Um... I've really been trying to keep up with things, I promise. But... I guess it has affected things a bit more than I'd like to admit. 

I actually haven't taken any of my freelance art-education work in a while. I just didn't want to let anyone down by doing a bad job, you know? And I haven't been going to my community events or soccer... which I feel so guilty about. 

As for around the house... I'm really embarrassed to say this, but my best friend actually has to come over and check on me a lot. I just... I forget to eat, and I haven't been showering as much as I should. She even worries about me keeping myself safe, which makes me feel like such a burden to her. I really hate that I'm not managing better. 

I'm sorry, I know I should be taking better care of myself. Does that... does that answer your question? I hope I'm not oversharing.
You mentioned your friend worries about you keeping yourself safe—can you tell me more about that? Have you had any thoughts of harming yourself or wishing you weren't alive?

Um... well... I don't want you to think I'm crazy or that I'm, like, a danger or anything. I really don't want to be a problem. But... I guess I have been having some thoughts. 

It's not that I want to do anything bad, I promise! It's just... sometimes I go to sleep and I just sort of... hope I don't wake up. Like it would just be easier for everyone if I wasn't here being such a mess. And... well, the other day, my friend came over and... I guess I didn't realize I was saying it out loud, but she heard me saying that I just couldn't keep living like this. 

I'm so sorry, I know that sounds terrible and I shouldn't think that way. I really am trying to be positive. Is... is it okay that I told you that? I just want to be honest so you can help me.

Before this current period started about 16 months ago, had you ever gone through a separate time in your life—perhaps for weeks or months—where you felt this same kind of deep sadness or loss of interest, followed by a period where you felt back to your normal self?

Um... let me think. I really want to give you the right answer here. 

Before this... no, I don't think so. I mean, everyone has bad days, right? I've definitely felt sad before, or had times where I was just feeling a little down, but... nothing like this. This heavy feeling, where it just doesn't stop for months and months... this is the first time it's ever been this bad. 

Before this started, I was usually pretty okay. I mean, I had my struggles, but I could always bounce back, you know? I was still doing my art and going to soccer. So... no, I haven't had a separate time like this before. 

Does that make sense? I hope I'm remembering everything right for you.
Have you ever had a period—lasting several days or more—where you felt unusually energetic, elated, or needed much less sleep than usual, along with being more talkative or impulsive than normal?

Um... no, I really don't think so. I've never been the type to be super energetic or, you know, overly talkative like that. 

I actually really rely on my sleep, so I've never had a time where I felt like I didn't need it. And I try very hard to be careful and not do impulsive things... I would really hate to cause any trouble or make bad decisions, you know? I always try to think things through. 

So, no, I haven't experienced anything like that. I hope that's okay? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information for your notes.
